I'm 42, been farming this land in Quzhou since I was young. I only finished primary school, but I know what works here. Everyone around me grows the wheat-corn rotation—that's the backbone of our farming. I planted winter wheat last October on most of my land, and now that spring is here, I need to topdress it and get the irrigation going. I'll harvest it in early June, then immediately put in summer corn. I also keep a small plot of cotton because the price can be good and I've grown it for years, though it takes more work.

I don't try anything fancy. I use rotary tillage before wheat planting, but for corn I plant no-till right into the wheat stubble—saves time and diesel. I buy hybrid corn seeds from the supply shop because they yield better, but for wheat I mostly use improved varieties I know. I fertilize with the compound blends from the local shop and irrigate from our well using border flooding. For pests, I spray when I see them—wheat and corn need a few sprays each, but cotton needs spraying almost every week.
